messages:
kai: Hey team — opened a small TF change that updates NAT gateway route propagation and adds a lifecycle ignore on the GPU ENI attachment resource. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/2143 Can someone take a look? Planning a staged rollout (staging -> prod canary).

infra-bot: CI: plan ✅, fmt ⚠️, validate ✅ — details: https://ci.redwood/internal/2143/plan

maya: @kai quick q — does this change the route table association for gpu-subnet-prod? If it touches associations we need a maintenance window.

kai: It only flips propagation on the transit-gateway attachment for prod-gpu-vpc, associations unchanged. No route table replacements. Intend to canary in staging first.

sam: Taking a look now :eyes: Which terraform workspace/vars should I run locally to repro the plan?

kai: use workspace=staging-gpu and the tfvars at infra/envs/staging-gpu.tfvars. Local repro: `TF_WORKSPACE=staging-gpu terraform plan -var-file=infra/envs/staging-gpu.tfvars`

jia: Also please add a short rollback note in the rollout doc about the ENI lifecycle and reattachment steps. Suggested snippet to include in the PR description:

```
resource "aws_network_interface" "gpu_eni" {
  lifecycle {
    ignore_changes = [attachment]
  }
}
```
This ensures TF won't detach/reattach ENIs during planned provider bumps.

sam: Left a small comment about pinning the aws provider to >= 4.50.0 in modules/gpu/provider.tf. FYI fmt warning is just a trailing newline in modules/gpu/main.tf.

maya: ok to approve once fmt is fixed and @eng-oncall signs off for prod rollouts. Please add a short note under Rollouts > gpu-network about the canary timing. :+1:

eng-oncall: pinged — I'm available for the prod canary window. Will check latency/attach metrics during canary.

infra-bot: Canary scheduled: 2026-03-19 02:00 UTC (pending approvals).

kai: pushed fixes for fmt and provider pin, updated PR description with rollback steps and rollout doc link. Marking as ready-for-review. Thanks all!
